notes: 1) The price and target are in GBp (pence). The model's figures are in EURm, so any comparison needs an FX conversion; the MarketScreener EUR-line figures (last €54.19, target €61.43) are a ready-made EUR equivalent. 2) Other aggregators disagree on the target: TipRanks averages 5,148.89p (Moderate Buy: 5 Buy / 3 Hold / 2 Sell), and Alpha Spread averages 5,520.01p (range 4,484.4–6,300p). Earlier Stockopedia snapshots showed 5,342.72p. 3) HYPERINFLATION TREATMENT BY ANALYSTS: there is no evidence that sell-side commentary separates the IAS 29 net monetary gain/(loss) from ordinary FX translation. The Q1 2026 call (Investing.com transcript) mentions Argentina and Türkiye only as volume stories ('high single digit growth in Argentina'; 'strong performances in markets such as India, Turkey, and Vietnam'), and currency comes up only as an aggregate headwind (CFO: 'FX reducing the reported turnover by 7.7%'). There are no mentions of hyperinflation or net monetary items. In the Q2 2026 call (28 Jul 2026), the only related analyst question was about Latin America pricing: 'pricing was obviously flat in the quarter despite the hyperinflations or contributions in the region ... is that done now?'. That frames hyperinflation as a pricing and underlying-sales-growth (USG) issue, not a net-monetary-position issue. Management described currency as having reduced H1 turnover by 4.9% and underlying EPS growth by about 6 percentage points, again as a single aggregate FX figure. Unilever's own USG methodology caps price growth in hyperinflationary economies (about 26%/yr, roughly 2%/month compounded), so the net monetary line stays out of the headline growth metric. This confirms the earlier note in valuation_inputs.json's consensus block: in practice the net monetary gain/(loss) is treated as a non-cash item folded into generic 'currency' and is not analysed separately. 4) LIMITATION: paywalled broker notes (e.g. Deutsche Bank, Barclays, Bernstein) were not accessible. This conclusion rests only on public transcripts, aggregators and Unilever's IR materials. 5) Web search turned up company-disclosed 2026 figures (a €299m hyperinflation adjustment for Argentina and Türkiye, and a net monetary loss of €68m for 2026 vs €201m for 2025). These come from Unilever's H1 2026 6-K and are recorded here as context only. They are NOT the model's figures. Per SOP, the model's authoritative values are in valuation_inputs.json (company_facts.net_monetary_gain_loss_eur = -195.0 EURm for 2024; ias29_impact_primary_year; monetary_exposure overall grade C), and later stages must use those, not these web figures. 6) The reference date equals today, so this is live research, not a backtest.
